idiom_name: tower Layer/Service middleware composed with axum Router::layer
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance, and the ecosystem answers with tower: the shared security sequence is a Layer/Service wrapping the router, or middleware::from_fn for application-local handlers, so every route the layer is applied to passes through it before the inner service runs. Identity and session state flow explicitly through request extensions rather than through a base type, and business handlers stay plain async functions. The classic structure is replaced by composition; implementing Service by hand is justified mainly for reusable, configurable middleware.
pitfalls: Router::layer wraps only the routes added before the call; routes registered afterwards are unguarded, so apply layers to the finished route tree or wrap the whole router.
Layer order is bottom-to-top with Router::layer but top-to-bottom with ServiceBuilder; mixing the two makes the security sequence implicit.
Middleware services must be Clone plus Send, and blocking work inside the async service stalls the executor.
